identity.title: ALMA Measurements of the HNC and HC<SUB>3</SUB>N Distributions in Titan's Atmosphere

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present spectrally and spatially-resolved maps of HNC and HC$_3$N emission from Titan’s atmosphere, obtained using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) on 2013 November 17.

evidence.quote: This resolution element corresponds to $4240\times2440$ km at Titan’s geocentric distance of 10.84 AU at the time of observation, compared to Titan’s mean radius of 2,576 km.

question.value: What are the spatial distributions and vertical abundance profiles of HNC and HC3N in Titan's atmosphere as seen by ALMA?

evidence.quote: Molecular emission maps and disk-averaged vertical mixing profiles are derived.
The article makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.A.00033.S.
a single 158 second integration of Titan was obtained using the dual-sideband Band 7 receiver.
The channel spacing was 244 kHz which (after Hanning smoothing by the correlator) produced a spectral resolution of 488 kHz (or $0.40$ km $\rm{s}^{-1}$ at 363 GHz).
Emission lines were detected from HNC $J=4-3$ at 362.630 GHz
The resulting spatial resolution (FWHM of the Gaussian restoring beam) was $0.54''\times0.31''$
The average RMS noise per channel was 31 mJy for HNC and 38 mJy for HC$_3$N.
a single 158 second integration of Titan was obtained
Observations of Titan were made on 2013 November 17 in Cycle 1 Early Science mode

what.value: Titan temperature profile from Cassini CIRS and HASI

pipeline_or_manual.value: Standard ALMA data reduction scripts by NA ALMA Science Center

evidence.quote: The data were flagged and calibrated by the North American ALMA Science Center using the standard data reduction scripts and protocols provided by the Joint ALMA Observatory.
The flux scale was determined by setting the observed continuum level to match the Butler-JPL-Horizons 2012 flux model for Titan
Absolute flux calibration is thus expected to be accurate to within 15%.
Titan’s strong, compact continuum permitted self-calibration of the phases.
Continuum subtraction and imaging were performed using standard routines in the NRAO CASA software version 4.2.0
Deconvolution (cleaning) of the ALMA point-spread function (PSF) was performed for each spectral channel using the Hogbom algorithm
with natural visibility weighting and a threshold flux level of twice the RMS noise
The image pixel sizes were set to $0.05\times0.05''$.
(long axis $57.3^{\circ}$ clockwise from celestial north)

method.value: Standard ALMA calibration, flux scaling to Titan model, continuum subtraction, Hogbom cleaning

analysis_steps.goal: Make integrated emission maps in Titan frame

method.value: Transform to projected distances and Titan rest frame; integrate ±1 km/s (HNC), ±5 km/s (HC3N)

evidence.quote: using integration ranges $\pm1.0$ km $\rm{s}^{-1}$ with respect to line center for HNC and $\pm5.0$ km $\rm{s}^{-1}$ for HC$_3$N.
using the JPL Horizons Topocentric radial velocity of $-0.91$ km $\rm{s}^{-1}$.

method.value: Integrate cubes over 1.5'' diameter circular aperture centered on Titan

evidence.quote: obtained by integrating the observed data cubes over a circular aperture $1.5''$ (12,000 km) in diameter, centered on Titan.

method.value: NEMESIS line-by-line radiative transfer with two-parameter gradient model (abundance at z_r=293 km, slope as fraction of scale height); HNC step model above 400 km

evidence.quote: A two-parameter ‘gradient model’ was used for the HNC and HC$_3$N vertical mixing ratio (VMR) profiles, with a variable abundance at reference altitude $z_r = 293$ km

key_parameters.value: 10-point trapezium-rule integration to model top at 782 km

evidence.quote: fluxes were calculated as a function of frequency using a 10-point trapezium-rule integration from the center of the disk to the edge of the model (at an altitude of 782 km).

assumptions.value: Profiles do not vary with latitude/longitude; HC3N condenses below ~71 km; Lorentz half-widths 1.290 (HNC), 0.1 (HC3N) cm-1/bar, exponents 0.69, 0.75

evidence.quote: The HC$_3$N was assumed to condense out at altitudes below $z_c \simeq 71$ km

fitting.value: chi^2 minimization between modeled and observed spectra

evidence.quote: Employing a $\chi^2$ minimization between the modeled and observed spectra

validation.value: Compared with previous VMR profiles (Marten, Teanby, Vinatier, Koskinen; Moreno 2012)

evidence.quote: Our HC$_3$N VMR profile is in reasonable agreement with these previous studies

analysis_steps.goal: Map HC3N line core vs wings

method.value: Integrate core (-0.5 to 0.5 km/s) and wings (2.0-5.0 km/s) separately to probe altitude

evidence.quote: just the line core ($-0.5$ to 0.5 km $\rm{s}^{-1}$) and (b) just the line wings (2.0 to 5.0 km $\rm{s}^{-1}$ either side of the line center)

$0.62 \pm 0.04$ ppb for HC$_3$N
$0.063 \pm 0.025$ ppb for HNC

findings_qualitative.value: HNC and HC3N emission are not co-spatial; HC3N peaks over poles, HNC offset

evidence.quote: Differences between the spectrally-integrated flux distributions of HNC and HC$_3$N show that these species are not co-spatial.

claims.hypothesis: Are HNC and HC3N distributions spatially the same?
claims.experiment: Integrated line maps from ALMA Band 7 cubes
claims.result: Double-peaked; HC3N peaks over poles, HNC offset 40±5 deg clockwise
claims.finding: Species are not co-spatial; mesosphere may be longitudinally variable

evidence.quote: indicating that the mesosphere may be more longitudinally-variable than previously thought.

claims.hypothesis: At what altitudes are HNC and HC3N found?
claims.experiment: NEMESIS fits to disk-averaged line profiles
claims.result: HNC at z≳400 km; HC3N across ~70-600 km
claims.finding: HNC confined to the upper atmosphere, HC3N broadly distributed

evidence.quote: HNC being concentrated predominantly in the mesosphere and above (at altitudes $z\gtrsim 400$ km)

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Diurnal chemical differentiation judged unlikely for HNC asymmetry because zonal winds mix longitudes in ~45 hr versus 382 hr day

evidence.quote: which renders diurnal chemical differentiation an unlikely explanation for the observed structures

limitations_admitted.value: Single line per species insufficient to constrain the true HNC distribution

evidence.quote: High signal-to-noise ratio observations of multiple emission lines could help constrain the true HNC distribution.

referee_caveats_inferred: Models assume no latitude/longitude variation despite resolved asymmetries
